newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha steady, eyes on KPC term talks.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha steady, eyes on KPC term talks.

text.p: Naphtha prices in Tokyo held steady, shrugging off bearish European naphtha markets as well losses in crude prices overnight, traders said.
"It's a bit surprising in a sense, especially as now we are hearing the West is weaker and crude prices are lower," one naphtha trader said.
He said naphtha's resilience probably means that the region's supply/demand balance for prompt cargoes has improved.
Term price talks between Kuwait and Asian naphtha buyers are scheduled to start next week in London.
About a dozen Japanese firms and four South Korean firms are expected to participate in the talks with Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) for one-year supply contracts starting in August.

Japanese lifters are likely to seek a premium of $13.50, the same price as one-year KPC term contracts that started in March, traders said. South Korea and Japan will buy about two million tonnes of Kuwaiti naphtha under the term contracts starting August, they said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half August was notionally quoted at $207.00/208.00 per tonne, while the first half of the month was notionally assessed about $1.00 lower.
